title: Dedicated node residency manifest export and tenant separation notarization
creator: Leah Thompson
description: Problem: Enterprise customers using Dedicated capacity require machine-verifiable manifests that prove a tenant's inference traffic was served from compliant geography, with tamper-evident records and retention controls. Current ad-hoc snapshots (logs + manual export) are insufficient for audits or contractual residency attestations.\n\nGoal: Build an automated manifest export and notarization pipeline that periodically captures a tenant-specific residency \"manifest\" (node IDs, AZ/region tags, kernel image, allocation IDs, timestamped KV cache pointers, and retention metadata), signs it with the Dedicated control-plane signing key, stores the manifest in the compliance vault, and publishes a compact notarization record that auditors can verify without exposing customer data. The pipeline must support configurable retention policies, per-tenant opt-in/export, RBAC, and an operator playbook for producing audit bundles on demand.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System can produce a signed residency manifest for a specific tenant that includes: list of serving node identifiers, region/AZ tags, model binary hash, start/end timestamps for the snapshot, and retention TTL metadata.
2) Each manifest is cryptographically signed using the Dedicated signing key (KMS-backed). Verification script validates signature and manifest hash deterministically.

3) Notarization record (manifest hash + signature + short metadata) is written to the compliance ledger S3 prefix and exposed via a read-only 'notary' API returning non-sensitive metadata for auditors.
4) Automated retention enforcement: manifests older than tenant-configured TTL are moved to cold archive or purged per policy; deletions are logged and captured in an immutable audit trail.
5) RBAC: Only customers with Dedicated entitlements and operators with compliance role can request on-demand bundles; API returns 403 otherwise.
6) End-to-end tests and load tests prove pipeline can create and notarize manifests for 500 tenants within a 30m maintenance window.
7) Documentation: Confluence runbook, sample verification script, and a template bundle for auditors are published and linked from the Console compliance panel.
8) Security review completed and signed-off by Security & Compliance team before GA.
9) Rollout: Feature behind a feature flag; gradual enablement for beta customers with telemetry to detect failures.
10) Observability: Traces, metrics, and alerting on signing failures, manifest generation latency, and S3 upload errors are in Console.
tasks: Design manifest schema (fields, redaction rules, canonical ordering) - RFC in Confluence
Implement manifest generator in dedicated-controlplane service (HTTP endpoint: /v1/tenants/{id}/residency-manifest)
Integrate KMS signing flow and verification helper (nodejs/python snippets for auditors)
Build notarization writer to compliance S3 prefix and lightweight notary API for metadata queries
Retention worker: TTL enforcement + cold-archive workflow + deletion confirmation events
RBAC checks wired into control-plane and console UI for on-demand bundle requests
Add observability: histogram for generation latency, counter for signed manifests, Sentry alert for signing errors
Write end-to-end tests and a load test harness for generating manifests at scale
Create Confluence runbook and sample auditor bundle; coordinate walkthrough with support/solutions
Security review and threat model update; address KMS rotation and key compromise recovery steps
